critique.model_split: upheld — Sonnet for A conditional on BLOCKING-1, -3 and -6 landing; Opus for B. Generalised for COST.md reuse: route on whether the acceptance is DECIDABLE WITHOUT JUDGEMENT at the time the agent writes it, not on how hard the subject sounds. Difficulty is not the axis, discretion is — A is the harder engineering job and the Sonnet one; B is mostly grep and is the Opus one because its central act is choosing a population, and two successive readers accepted an uncounted premise about that population. Headline corollary: the plan loop CONVERTS OPUS BUILDS INTO SONNET BUILDS by manufacturing the three conditions PLAN-LOOP's middle row requires — so COST.md levers 1 and 4 should be measured as ONE coupled lever, and that is the largest uncosted saving in the programme. Critics stay Opus unconditionally; downgrading a critic is the same cut as removing one.

critique.carried_6_closed: sabotage.mjs has NO expected-side slot: runControl's measure() returns {value, support, detail?} and arms store {arm,broken,value,support,support_declared,detail,error,canon,measured_nothing} (lib/sabotage.mjs:333-360). spec.expect is an expected VERDICT not an expected NUMBER; spec.margin/direction declare a relation between arms; spec.detail is free-form and stashing E there is the loose-convention defect the module was rebuilt to prevent. Ruling S-PLAN-HUD-B STANDS (verdict on the facility, not a new tool) because the blast radius is 9 files referencing runControl, but the plan must price the contract change: a new absent-is-a-verdict sibling to support, a validateSpec change, a VERDICT entry, and exit code 12 (EXIT_FOR uses 0,2-7,10,11; 8 and 9 are the CLI's). It is the TENTH verdict, not the sixth as the plan's section 3 says.

dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.at_commit: 9063779 (pinned via git archive to a snapshot outside the repo; the working tree gained six tools/**/*.mjs from other agents during the run)
dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.where: orchestration/plans/W1-HUD-TOAST.md — section 'MEASUREMENT — the quoted-E fraction', the last section of the file; a CLOSED pointer sits on the dispatch-condition paragraph itself
dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.headline: quoted-E fraction = 14 of 109 = 12.8%. Under the strict reading of the claim it tests — a bar the verdict graded against AT THE TIME it believed the result — 3 of 109 = 2.8%, and one of those three is a verdict recording that it does not know which bar applies.
dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.counting_rule: A tool counts as E-QUOTED iff a wave-1 verdict DOCUMENT (never the artifacts/ subtree, which holds 112 copied tool sources) states a specific expected value for a NAMED GRADED ROW of that tool, in the enclosing prose block (a blank-line paragraph in .md, one JSON string value in .json). Value may be numeric or a literal ([], false, true, ERROR). EXCLUDED: outcome words with no value (exits 0, passes, green); observed readings (that is O, which YD already has); N/N self-test tallies (the bar is 'all of them' and the denominator is the tool's own); command lines and artifact listings; descriptive population sizes; directional expectations (must rise) with no arm value; and a bar the verdict explicitly restates from the tool's own source. COUNTED as borderlines: non-numeric literals, categorical row-values, a reference item's bar, and one contested bar.
dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.method: census of all 109, not a sample. 17 tools had no numeric prose context and 10 were cited only in command/artifact listings; all 27 were read anyway for digit-free literal expectations. The remaining 82 were read in full context and ruled by hand. A 40-tool sample taken first gave 5/40 with a Wilson upper edge of 26.1% straddling the decision boundary, and the census then CORRECTED the sample on critic-road-join-ingame.mjs.

dispatch_condition_for_piece_B.gradeability_verdict: B1 AS WRITTEN IS NOT GRADEABLE. The <25% branch of the revised reversibility condition fires. But the reason is sharper than the fraction and should replace it in the brief: B1's acceptance is '100% of P classified into {INDEPENDENT, COUPLED, INERT, OPAQUE, ERROR}', every member can always be assigned one of five classes, and OPAQUE is one of them — so B1 CANNOT GO RED. On this population OPAQUE is modal by construction (95 of 109 have no external E). B1 would score 100% while establishing nothing: an acceptance that cannot fail, inside the piece written to sweep for acceptances that cannot fail.

The ~9% line-adjacency proxy was not pessimistic, it was optimistic. Eleven of the fourteen E-QUOTED cases sit in biggest_gap.remedy.acceptance — a bar written for the NEXT round's fix, not the bar the verdict used.

rulings_rule_0_added_by_the_measurement.ruling: Execute exchange 1's <25% branch, but re-denominate rather than delete. B1' (graded) runs over P_E = the 14 tools for which a wave-1 verdict states an external expected value for a named row (list committed in the plan's MEASUREMENT section). Acceptance: 100% of 14 classified INDEPENDENT/COUPLED/INERT/ERROR with the tool's own E and the verdict's frozen E printed per row; OPAQUE is NOT an available outcome because an external E exists by construction for every member. COUPLED count published over the denominator 14, never as a bare percentage. 14 clears exchange 1's own floor of ~8. B1b (reported, never graded) keeps the wide denominator 109, of which 95 (87.2%) have no external E. B2 unchanged and still the acceptance.
